claims.text: The baseline material is FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy-alloy powder with a 15–45 μm feedstock size deposited using HVAF-i7.
The baseline HVAF-i7 process produces acceptable coating quality but insufficient coating thickness.
Increasing particle velocity during HVAF-i7 deposition will overcome the coating-thickness limitation.
Reducing the nozzle-to-substrate distance toward 300–350 mm can increase particle velocity in the HVAF-i7 process.
Increasing propellant flow or pressure can increase particle velocity in the HVAF-i7 process.
Higher particle velocity increases the particles' in-flight kinetic energy.
Higher particle velocity improves in-flight melting of FeCoNiCrAl particles.
Higher particle velocity improves particle impact, flattening, and splat formation on the substrate.
Improved particle melting and splatting produce better coating adhesion.
Improved particle melting and splatting increase deposited thickness per pass.
The increased-velocity process will produce a denser coating.
The increased-velocity process will reduce in-spray oxidation.
The intervention will produce a significantly thicker and adherent bond coat than the baseline HVAF-i7 process using 15–45 μm feedstock.
The thicker coating will retain minimal oxidation and durability during high-temperature service.
The intervention should remain effective for deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
An approximately 300–350 mm nozzle-to-substrate distance is an effective operating range for this HVAF-i7 FeCoNiCrAl intervention.
Differences in torch design and spray dynamics may prevent HVAF-i7 from achieving the particle-velocity increase reported for M3 processing of conventional MCrAlY coatings.
